Retrieved 2026-07-20 via Exa search highlights.

Zelensky's surprise government reshuffle: parliament approved new Cabinet under PM Serhii Koretskyi (former Naftogaz CEO) on 16 July. Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov (35, tech reformer, appointed Jan 2026, ~6-7 months in post) NOT reappointed after acrimonious clash with Army C-in-C Gen Oleksandr Syrskyi. Ousting triggered rare "cardboard" street protests across Ukraine and solidarity statements from senior commanders. Fedorov said his removal was triggered by Syrskyi presenting Zelensky with an ultimatum.

Both Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha and Defence Minister posts fell vacant automatically under Ukrainian law. Zelensky named SBU acting chief Yevhen Khmara as acting defence minister (career intelligence officer behind long-range strike ops / Alpha special forces) — but legality questioned (president cannot appoint acting defence minister; that is the Cabinet's role). Cabinet formally appointed Khmara and Sybiha as acting heads evening of 17 July after a day of legal limbo. Formal appointments need Rada approval; parliament in recess until 18 August, no vote scheduled.

Also: Zelensky proposed former Interior Minister Ihor Klymenko as new secretary of National Security and Defence Council (NSDC), replacing Rustem Umerov (who led Ukraine's delegation to stalled US-Russia peace talks; his next role unclear).
